title: Psalm Puzzle Booth
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
At a Christian homeschool co-op fair in a rented convention hall, Peter ran a paid Bible-verse puzzle booth without the required county amusement permit, a misdemeanor. Ruth bought a ticket, completed the puzzle, collected a bookmark, and left. Later that afternoon, while helping Stephen hang a banner at a bakery for a separate youth-group fundraiser, Ruth stood on a defective stepstool, fell, and died. Peter was charged with involuntary manslaughter based on operating the booth without the permit.

Is Peter guilty of misdemeanor manslaughter?
call: Is Peter guilty of misdemeanor manslaughter?

choices.A: No, because operating the unpermitted puzzle booth did not actually or proximately cause Ruth’s fall from the stepstool.
choices.B: Yes, because Peter was committing a misdemeanor when he operated the puzzle booth.
choices.C: No, because misdemeanor manslaughter applies only to violent misdemeanors.
choices.D: Yes, because any death after a misdemeanor is involuntary manslaughter.

rightExplanation: A is correct. The charged theory is misdemeanor manslaughter based on the unpermitted puzzle booth. The booth did not produce, set up, or increase the risk of Ruth’s later fall from a defective stepstool at a different location. Gold Key: misdemeanor manslaughter still needs actual and proximate causation; a misdemeanor that merely happened earlier is not enough. Silver Key: when one answer links the misdemeanor to the death and another only names the misdemeanor, choose the cause-link answer.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: not responsive. It proves the misdemeanor only. It does not connect the misdemeanor to Ruth’s death.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: not true. “Any death after a misdemeanor” is an absolute chronology rule. The answer overclaims.

c3.label: CUT C
c3.text: anchor-assisted not true. It invents a violent-only threshold. The better no-liability reason is causation.

c3.label: Residual
c3.text: A. It is true and responsive after the Gold Key is applied. No Clash or Call needed.

studentScript: The call asks misdemeanor manslaughter. The misdemeanor is the unpermitted booth. Ruth died later from a stepstool fall. Gold Key: misdemeanor manslaughter needs actual and proximate cause. Cut the label-only answer, cut the any-death overclaim, cut the violent-only threshold. A remains.

A.signal: This choice connects the charged misdemeanor to the death mechanism and says the link is missing.
A.lawyer: Correct under misdemeanor-manslaughter causation. The unpermitted booth did not actually or proximately cause the stepstool fall.

B.signal: It proves the unlawful act but does not connect that act to Ruth’s death.
B.lawyer: The predicate misdemeanor alone does not establish misdemeanor manslaughter; causation remains required.

C.signal: It ignores the cause-link fact and substitutes a violent-only rule.
C.lawyer: The decisive defect is not that the misdemeanor was nonviolent; the defect is lack of actual and proximate causation.

D.signal: The word 'any' turns a cause rule into a pure timeline rule.
D.lawyer: Misdemeanor manslaughter is not strict liability for every later death; actual and proximate cause remain required.

goldKeys.statement: Misdemeanor manslaughter still needs actual and proximate causation. A misdemeanor that merely happens before a death is not enough.
goldKeys.trigger: unlawful act followed by a separate death mechanism
goldKeys.authority: MPC §2.03; People v. Penny; Logan/Ceasar line reflected in Oklahoma jury-instruction commentary

silverKeys.statement: When the array gives you a misdemeanor-label answer and a cause-link answer, lock the cause link before debating the label.
silverKeys.trigger: one choice says the misdemeanor happened; another choice says the misdemeanor did not cause the death

remediation.title: Misdemeanor label is not a death cause
remediation.signal: A misdemeanor is followed by a death from a separate event.
remediation.studentMove: Ask whether the misdemeanor produced the death, not merely whether it came first.
remediation.tinyRule: No cause link, no misdemeanor manslaughter.
